scope: Native private identity enrollment, one-time bootstrap, hostname changes and CLI credential staging; no packet-service activation or URM2 rollout

verification.user_service_test_executable: Previously built CLI-publication release; production checks execute the newly packaged native CLI

checks: Enrollment, hostname and bootstrap validation match retained original model fixtures
Enrollment preserves existing peer IDs and addresses, while custom-name clearing restores the assigned machine label
Concurrent one-time ticket claims yield exactly one private credential
Reissued native generations reject stale capabilities, revoked issuers cannot redeem, and pending Go tickets without generation fields remain supported
Short links negotiate private metadata and select the native enroll command without exposing public machine credentials
New private profiles retain the existing Go wire fields and are stored privately without overwriting files
CLI rejects redirects, identity mismatch, plaintext without the explicit test flag, unsafe destinations and cancellation before ticket consumption
Actual CLI reads long tickets from stdin and omits tokens and gateway addresses from ordinary output
Packaged production CLI stages two private identities through real API-issued capabilities and the native API exchanges and acknowledges a scoped offer
Previous public file transfer, firewall, diagnostics, retirement and restart checks remain passing
limitations: Private enrollment stages credentials only; no private TUN, packet service or shared CLI publication from the private first-download launcher is activated
The one-time exchange is not crash-recoverable after an ambiguous successful response or failed credential save; revoke/reissue is required in that case
Native gateway relay, TUN/DNS/ICE/DTLS transport, certificate-possession proof and background path selection remain incomplete
Private group mutation, legacy installer aliases/service takeover, platform lifecycle and crash-safe updates remain outstanding
No private payload connectivity or final physical throughput is proved
No commit, push, URM2 deployment, registered-agent upgrade or final physical-machine benchmark performed
